String contains method with regex=True ignores flags parameter

#### Description

```python
import numpy as np
import re

# Test case 1: flags parameter ignored
data = pd.Series(['dave@google.com', 'steve@gmail.com', 'rob@gmail.com'])
pat = '([A-Z0-9._%+-]+)@([A-Z0-9.-]+)\\.([A-Z]{2,4})'

# This should match with IGNORECASE flag but doesn't work as expected
result = data.str.contains(pat, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
print("With flags=re.IGNORECASE:", result.tolist())
# Expected: [True, True, True] but gets different result

# Test case 2: case parameter behavior inconsistent
ser = pd.Series(['ab', 'AB', 'abc', 'ABC'])
result1 = ser.str.contains('AB', case=False)
result2 = ser.str.contains('AB', case=False, regex=True)
print("case=False, regex=False:", result1.tolist())
print("case=False, regex=True:", result2.tolist())
# These should give same results but don't
```

The issue seems to affect the logic flow where regex and non-regex code paths are getting mixed up, causing flags to be ignored when regex=True.
